description: A single-panel Ashby-style scatter plot (no sub-panels), plotting "Product of strength and ductility (GPa %)" on the y-axis (5 to 50, gridlines every 5) against "Density (g/cm³)" on the x-axis (6.2 to 8.0, ticks every 0.2). A 16-entry legend at the right identifies every material by marker shape and colour: 0.5Be (dark square), 1.0Be (red circle), 1.5Be (blue triangle), Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr (green down-triangle), Fe-28Mn-9Al-1.2C-9Cr (purple diamond), Fe-28Mn-12Al-1.2C (olive left-triangle), Fe-3.5Mn-5Al-0.25C (cyan right-triangle), Fe-10Mn-5Al-0.25C (brown hexagon), Fe-0.07C-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.12Si (olive star), 40Cr (orange pentagon), GCr15 (cyan circle), 12CrNi3A (green cross), 0Cr13 (grey X), 1Cr23Ni18 (red asterisk), 50CrVA (blue dash) and Q235 (green dash). A red shaded ellipse labelled "Be steel / Fe-30Mn-10Al-1.5C-(0.5-1.5)Be" encloses the three Be-steel points, which sit at the far-left (lowest density, ~6.2-6.45 g/cm³) and span from about the 20 GPa % gridline up to the highest point of the whole plot, the 0.5Be square, above the 45 GPa % gridline. A dashed black envelope curve marks the upper bound of the property space, and a "Low density" label with a red leftward arrow indicates the direction of density reduction. The conventional steels (40Cr, GCr15, 12CrNi3A, 0Cr13, 1Cr23Ni18, 50CrVA, Q235) cluster at the high-density, low-product corner near 7.7-7.9 g/cm³ and ≤25 GPa %. The figure demonstrates that Be steels combine the lowest density of any material plotted with a high strength-ductility product.

subfigures.description: Scatter (Ashby) plot of product of strength and ductility (GPa %) vs density (g/cm³), 16 labelled materials, a red shaded 'Be steel' ellipse for Fe-30Mn-10Al-1.5C-(0.5-1.5)Be, a dashed envelope curve and a 'Low density' arrow annotation.

observations.observation: The plot's y-axis is labelled 'Product of strength and ductility (GPa %)' over the range 5 to 50, and the x-axis 'Density (g/cm³)' over 6.2 to 8.0.
A red shaded ellipse is labelled 'Be steel' and 'Fe-30Mn-10Al-1.5C-(0.5-1.5)Be' and encloses the three Be-steel data points at the lowest densities on the plot (left of the 6.5 g/cm³ gridline).

Within the Be-steel ellipse, 0.5Be (dark square) is the highest point of the entire figure, lying between the 45 and 50 GPa % gridlines, 1.0Be (red circle) lies between the 30 and 35 gridlines and 1.5Be (blue triangle) lies between the 20 and 25 gridlines.

The 16 legend entries comprise the Be steels 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be; light Fe-Mn-Al-C steels Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr, Fe-28Mn-9Al-1.2C-9Cr, Fe-28Mn-12Al-1.2C, Fe-3.5Mn-5Al-0.25C, Fe-10Mn-5Al-0.25C, Fe-0.07C-11.15Mn-5.6Al-0.12Si; and the conventional steels 40Cr, GCr15, 12CrNi3A, 0Cr13, 1Cr23Ni18, 50CrVA, Q235.

Conventional high-strength steels (40Cr, GCr15, 12CrNi3A, 0Cr13, 1Cr23Ni18, 50CrVA, Q235) plot at the highest densities, beyond the 7.6 g/cm³ gridline, with strength-ductility products at or below the 25 GPa % gridline.

A dashed black curve defines the upper envelope of the plotted property space, running from about the 6.4 g/cm³ / 10 GPa % corner up to a maximum near the 7.6 g/cm³ gridline at about the 40 GPa % gridline before falling again.
A 'Low density' text annotation with a red leftward-pointing arrow is drawn in the lower-left region of the plot (near 6.3-6.5 g/cm³, ~7-8 GPa %), indicating the direction of decreasing density.
The caption states the figure compares the mechanical properties and density relationship of Be steels with other existing high-strength metal materials.
The citing text states the density of the Be steel is 21.38% lower than that of pure iron; no numeric density value for pure iron is printed on the plot itself.
The citing text states the comparison is made on the product of density, tensile strength and elongation (strong plastic product), which corresponds to the plotted y-quantity.
No numeric data labels are printed next to any data point; all point values must be read against the gridlines.

unreadable_items: Exact coordinates of every data point: no numeric labels are printed, so positions are only resolvable to the nearest gridline
Marker shapes of the closely spaced high-density points (12CrNi3A, 0Cr13, 50CrVA, Q235, 40Cr around 7.7-7.9 g/cm³) are difficult to distinguish at the supplied resolution
